name: alt-nfp
what_it_holds: Bayesian state-space nowcasting system for US nonfarm payrolls combining CES survey prints, QCEW administrative anchors, private payroll-provider microdata, and cyclical indicators, with 'strict as-of censoring' so backtests only see what was knowable on the day (true real-time/ALFRED-style vintage reconstruction). Pipeline stages: lookups -> download -> ingest -> vintages; model layer in JAX/NumPyro; data persisted to S3-compatible storage with local fallback. MIT-licensed.
why_useful: A working point-in-time vintage-reconstruction pipeline for BLS employment series (CES+QCEW) -- directly on-point for CONTEXT.md gap #4 (ALFRED-style macro vintages) and gap #17 (nowcasting methods/mixed-frequency). Could be adapted to isolate the leisure & hospitality CES/QCEW sub-series as a vintage-correct labor-cost/employment input.
geography: US, national (industry detail depends on config)
time_coverage: not stated explicitly; built for real-time vintage backtesting
size_hint: codebase + pipeline, no flat data files committed
themes: Hospitality labour and cost data: BLS QCEW/CES leisure and hospitality, hotel wages, cleaning-service prices, STR operating cost datasets
why_all: A working point-in-time vintage-reconstruction pipeline for BLS employment series (CES+QCEW) -- directly on-point for CONTEXT.md gap #4 (ALFRED-style macro vintages) and gap #17 (nowcasting methods/mixed-frequency). Could be adapted to isolate the leisure & hospitality CES/QCEW sub-series as a vintage-correct labor-cost/employment input.

name: UPGo-McGill/ghost
what_it_holds: Standalone R package (spun out of strr) implementing the 'ghost hotel/hostel' detector: identifies clusters of private-room STR listings that are actually being run as a single commercial operation out of one building/unit.
why_useful: A concrete, published algorithm for flagging commercial/illegal operators in an Inside Airbnb-style panel — could be run against our own 13-city or 120-market Inside Airbnb cohort to build a professional-host / supply-quality signal.
themes: University and municipal research datasets on STRs published on GitHub (city planning departments, urban labs, McGill UPGo, Inside Airbnb collaborators)
UPGo (McGill) and strr R package: STR research tooling and datasets for Canada/US cities
why_all: A concrete, published algorithm for flagging commercial/illegal operators in an Inside Airbnb-style panel — could be run against our own 13-city or 120-market Inside Airbnb cohort to build a professional-host / supply-quality signal.
Methodology for detecting commercial/illegal STR operators, relevant to gap #12 (regulatory/registration compliance) and to separating true P2P supply from de facto hotel supply within STR panels.
Could be applied to our Inside Airbnb panel to estimate the commercial/multi-listing share of supply, a proxy for professionalised vs. casual host mix that feeds nights/ADR interpretation.

name: UPGo-McGill/raffle
what_it_holds: Standalone R package implementing the 'raffle' method: probabilistically assigns STR listings (given only an approximate/obfuscated map point, as Airbnb/AirDNA show) to administrative geography (city, neighbourhood, census tract) by weighted random assignment matching known listing-density priors.
why_useful: Method for geocoding fuzzy STR listing locations into standard geographies, useful for building regional (city/neighbourhood-level) STR supply panels from Inside-Airbnb-style data with imprecise coordinates.
themes: University and municipal research datasets on STRs published on GitHub (city planning departments, urban labs, McGill UPGo, Inside Airbnb collaborators)
UPGo (McGill) and strr R package: STR research tooling and datasets for Canada/US cities
why_all: Method for geocoding fuzzy STR listing locations into standard geographies, useful for building regional (city/neighbourhood-level) STR supply panels from Inside-Airbnb-style data with imprecise coordinates.

Reusable geocoding method for our own Inside Airbnb 123-market panel, where Airbnb's public listing lat/long is deliberately jittered — could sharpen neighbourhood-level assignment for regional/city splits.

name: FlowKit
what_it_holds: Flowminder's open-source CDR (call detail record) analytics toolkit: a full pipeline (Spark backend, FlowAPI, FlowClient Python/R clients, FlowAuth) for turning raw mobile operator CDRs into mobility indicators (flows, residential/relocation, subscriber density, event counts) at scale. No data committed (operates on an operator's own CDR store) but a mature, actively maintained (98 stars, updated Aug 2026), MPL-2.0-licensed method for exactly the kind of MNO-derived mobility indicator Eurostat's experimental tourism statistics use.
why_useful: This is the reference open-source implementation of the MNO-mobility-indicator pipeline (used in real national statistics offices for humanitarian/mobility work); documents the exact indicator definitions (home location, trips, subscriber density) that a from-scratch MNO tourism proxy would need, even though we would still need our own CDR/roaming source to run it.
geography: global (framework, not tied to one country)
themes: Electricity, water and waste data as occupancy proxies (smart-meter open data, tourist-area utility consumption), and mobile-phone tourism statistics (Eurostat MNO experimental)
why_all: This is the reference open-source implementation of the MNO-mobility-indicator pipeline (used in real national statistics offices for humanitarian/mobility work); documents the exact indicator definitions (home location, trips, subscriber density) that a from-scratch MNO tourism proxy would need, even though we would still need our own CDR/roaming source to run it.

name: revmng
what_it_holds: Python library for hotel/airline revenue management: single-leg seat/room protection (Littlewood rule, EMSR-a/b, exact dynamic programming), overbooking, pricing, group displacement, length-of-stay controls, network bid prices. No committed booking-pace data, but validated against published worked examples (textbook RM cases) and could be used to build a synthetic OTB/pickup forward-curve model from disclosed occupancy/ADR to sanity-check pace assumptions.
why_useful: Directly relevant to gap 17 (methods: nowcasting/RM methodology) and to the booking-curve/forward-curve theme even though it carries no proprietary data itself — useful for structuring a pickup model against the ~60%-booked-before-quarter-start framing in CONTEXT.
themes: Booking-curve / pace / pickup datasets for hotels and STRs (on-the-books, forward bookings), Key Data / Transparent / Lighthouse (OTA Insight) samples, revenue-management forward curves
Hotel and STR supply from CoStar/CBRE/JLL/Cushman public reports scraped; real-estate broker STR reports with data
why_all: Directly relevant to gap 17 (methods: nowcasting/RM methodology) and to the booking-curve/forward-curve theme even though it carries no proprietary data itself — useful for structuring a pickup model against the ~60%-booked-before-quarter-start framing in CONTEXT.

Could supply a validated RM/bid-price modeling framework for thinking about ADR/occupancy trade-offs and length-of-stay dynamics (methods for gap #17 nowcasting/analogue kernels), not a data source itself.

Pure methods tooling (no data) that implements the RevPAR/ADR-pricing mechanics hotels and STR operators use; could inform how to model ADR/occupancy trade-offs mechanically, but contributes nothing toward the CoStar/CBRE/JLL data gap directly.
